title: Map the misconceptions before teaching
statement: Before teaching a concept, write down its end-of-course target, each known misconception with its persistence, cost and origin, when each framework teaches it, and the riskiest points in the sequence.
detail: The science misconception guidance in the curriculum folder gives each concept a card with the same parts: the target students must ultimately reach, a map of each misconception rated by persistence and impact with its origin, a trace of when and how each framework teaches the concept, and the highest-risk points in the teaching sequence (`downloads/5. Curriculum/Texts/Misconception and alignment checks/Science/Chemistry Misconception Prevention Guidance.docx`, lines 6-9). In the maps, impact is what a misconception costs on the AP exam and origin is where it comes from, such as textbooks, everyday language or documentaries (`downloads/5. Curriculum/Texts/Misconception and alignment checks/Science/Biology Misconception Prevention Guidance.docx`, lines 9-18). The guides rank concepts on different grounds, biology by exam weight and chemistry by how foundational a concept is, so no ranking rule is claimed (Biology line 5, Chemistry line 15).
